title: A first-time user's plan, run and landing do what they said
description: Testbed faults from the danuvia-software run on 3.2.0: F588, F589, F595, F591, F594, F593. Each was hit by a real first-time user.
desiredOutcome: On a fresh repo a first phase is planned in one verb call with no placeholder, /audit:run never runs less or more than the user named, a stopped drive leaves no lock behind, the gate's evidence lands in the project's own directory, and a single-checkout landing leaves the user on the branch the work landed on.

tasks.title: a missing plan is created by the first /audit:phase add, with no placeholder task
tasks.description: F588: on a repo with no plan, /audit:phase add hits _under_lock's 'manifest not found -- run /audit:init first' (exit 2), and the model went into the plugin's source, found seed, created the plan, retargeted the seeded phase, cancelled seed's placeholder and added tasks: 16 turns, 0.83 USD to plan two tasks. F589: _locked_seed hardcodes P1 with a placeholder task P1.1. Make add-phase and the batch add (add --from-file) seed a missing plan themselves (seed's meta, the requested phase as the first phase, no placeholder), and give seed a --no-task form; the missing-manifest refusal stays for the task verbs that need an existing phase. Mind fb10 (phase.md's add section is pinned to at most 8000 bytes and to its heredoc) and test__refs' flag/hint parity. Say it in phase.md, init.md, verbs-in-full.md, README.md's /audit:init and /audit:phase rows, and QUICKSTART.md's cheaper-first-step paragraph.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_task.py: add-phase and add --from-file on a project with no manifest write the plan (seed's meta and index) and exactly the requested phase and tasks in one call, with no placeholder task; seed --no-task writes no task

outcome.technical: audit-task.py: _under_lock gained create=True (used by cmd_phase_add and _cmd_batch_add); on a missing plan _create_then writes an empty plan from _seed_meta, runs the body, removes the file unless the body returned 0. seed gained --no-task (VERB_FLAGS, parser, _locked_seed). Task verbs still refuse a missing plan. Docs: phase.md (kept the run form at exactly the 4000 ceiling, one short line), init.md, verbs-in-full.md, README.md two rows, QUICKSTART.md. New stage fp-block with fp1-fp6 in test_audit_task.py. Full test_audit_task selftest was 950/951 only because of fb15 (the measure-context ceiling), which I fixed; fb-block+fp-block rerun 22/22; test__refs 334/334; the full selftest was not rerun after the fix.
outcome.descriptive: A first phase on a repo with no plan is created in one verb call with no placeholder task; seed gets --no-task.

redFirst.basis: `python3 plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_task.py --selftest --stage fp-block` in a throwaway tree at HEAD exited 1 with failing cases fp1 (house FAIL), fp2 (house FAIL), fp6 (house FAIL), but HEAD's own tests on HEAD's code are not green (SELFTEST FAILED: 0/1 cases passed) - the command is already red (or unreadable) at HEAD - narrow it to the task's cases - SELFTEST FAILED: 3/6 cases passed; run without CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR; dependencies linked from the project root, entry by entry as symlinks: node_modules - .cache, .vite, .vite-temp are not linked and a new entry a runner makes beside the links stays in the throwaway, but a write into a linked entry lands in the project's own node_modules and is not watched; the user's .npmrc in the home directory dropped (every run has a fresh home)

tasks.title: a drive that stops releases the phase lock it took
tasks.description: F591: drive-phase.drive calls take_lock first; when audit-task start (or done, record_gate, commit_signoff, land) exits non-zero, drive_task and drive_phase return the stop directly and the lock is released only in finish/finish_task, reached only on done. So any stop after take_lock strands phase-<id>, which status later reads as abandoned. Release on every stop path that this invocation took the lock on (one exit point, not one release per arm), and give an index-lock exit 3 from audit-task its own followed rule instead of the generic 'stopped'. Keep STEPS in step with the README's followed table if a rule is added (_refs.followed_anchor_drift). Update orchestrator.md's concurrency-lock release rule.

tasks.title: /audit:run given a phase id refuses and names /audit:phase
tasks.description: F595: the owner typed /audit:run p1 meaning the phase; P1.2 alone ran. On main, run.md hands the argument to drive-phase next, whose context tries resolve_phase_id first, so a phase id drives the WHOLE phase (pinned by dt3) - the opposite of the observation. Establish first, from the testbed session's transcript, whether the script or the model picked P1.2, and write the answer into the task note. Either way /audit:run's contract is one task: add a one-task form to drive-phase next (a flag run.md passes) that refuses a phase-shaped id with one line naming /audit:phase <id> and the tasks it would run (in waves once F600 lands, one at a time before), and never picks a task. /audit:phase keeps next <phaseId>. dt3 stays true for the phase form. Update run.md, verbs-in-full.md and README.md's /audit:run row.

tasks.title: a single-checkout landing leaves the checkout on the branch it landed on
tasks.description: F594: merge_plan's no-checkout mode fast-forwards the parent ref with fetch . branch:refs/heads/parent and never moves HEAD, and commit_landing then commits the stamp and journal rows on the phase branch and fast-forwards the parent again. The user stays on the merged phase branch and starts the next phase from it. When the landing runs in the checkout that holds the phase branch, the parent is held by no worktree and that checkout is clean, switch it to the parent after the merge and commit the landing there; otherwise keep today's behaviour and say plainly that the checkout still sits on the merged branch, with the git switch command. phase-signoff.md documents 'It never moves your HEAD' - check COMPATIBILITY.md before changing a documented promise, and rewrite that sentence and the mt0-mt2 / ns3 expectations to the new rule rather than adding an exception beside them.

tasks.title: run-test-gate resolves its project the way every other verb does
tasks.description: F593, PRIORITY (hit the testbed owner twice; root cause reproduced, see PLAN.md F593). Two resolvers answer 'which project does this manifest belong to': _evidence_io.project_config_for (--project-dir, CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, then the MANIFEST'S OWN DIRECTORY) used by run-test-gate._own_log_dir, and _panel_write.project_of_manifest (first ancestor holding .claude/ or .git). The first hand-run gate (no CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR in a terminal or Bash-tool shell) writes its raw log under docs/audit/.claude/, which then makes project_of_manifest answer docs/audit forever, so every later run without --project-dir records evidence into docs/audit/docs/audit/, which no check reads. Every printed gate remedy omits --project-dir (commit-task-work's, audit-task's gate_command and its other print sites). Fix the class: ONE project resolver for every writer and every printed command, anchored on the git toplevel (or a .git file), never accepting a .claude/ marker inside the manifest's own docs/audit-shaped directory; project_config_for's manifest-dir fallback goes away; printed commands then need no flag because the default is right; keep audit-task.resolve_basis and drive-phase.project_context on the same function. Add a doctor hygiene check naming a stray <manifest dir>/.claude or docs/audit/docs. Keep lp1 true. Blocked by P123.1 only because both edit audit-task.py. ALSO (F537, the same class): Fold F537 into P123.5: render-report takes CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR or the manifest's own directory (<T>/docs/audit, not <T>) for its project, and audit-status takes CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR or the cwd for project and git root (so /audit:status from another checkout answers every phase's full-run question 'unknown'); both go through the one resolver P123.5 builds, verbs-in-full.md's '/audit:status asks git from CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, or the directory it runs in' sentence is rewritten, and an _output lint flags a project derived from a manifest path by dirname arithmetic (prove-gates row). Regression: a default-layout manifest rendered with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR unset reads <T>'s evidence; status run with cwd in another checkout reads the plan's own checkout. Also add F593's RECURRED shape as a case: run-test-gate given a RELATIVE manifest and no --project-dir records into <root>/docs/audit/evidence, never docs/audit/docs/audit. Because P123.5 now edits _output.py, test__output.py and tools/prove-gates.py, it needs dependsOn P123.6-z4y (shared _output.py/test__output.py) besides the P123.1 order its description already states.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_run_test_gate.py: a fresh repo plus one hand-run gate with no flags and no CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, then a second run: both land in <root>/docs/audit/evidence, and no <manifest dir>/.claude or docs/audit/docs is created

tasks.title: a failing tool's output is excerpted head and tail with the failure lines kept, through one helper
tasks.description: F598 + F553, one class from opposite ends: _scoped_commit cuts every refusal reason to (err or out).strip()[:200] (head only), so danuvia's lint-staged refusal kept the progress preamble and lost the failing check; verify.sh keeps only the tail of a failing step, so a failing vitest test could not be named. Choosing an end is the bug. Add one helper in a new scripts/_excerpt.py (L1; the five things CLAUDE.md lists for a new .py): head and tail of a failing tool's output with an explicit 'N chars elided' marker between, plus the lines matching a failure shape (✖, error, FAIL, ERR_) from the elided middle. Route every subprocess-output refusal reason through it: _scoped_commit's (the most cuts), _ado_fetch and _ado_connect's, and any other site in scripts/ that cuts git or tool OUTPUT (a title or a summary cut is a different thing and stays); journal rows keep the excerpt whole in details and clip only the summary (_journal_io._clip_marked). verify.sh's failing-step print keeps every FAIL/✖ line plus the tail. Add a lint in _output.py banning a bare .strip()[:N] / [:N] on a name bound from subprocess output, with a red-first allow case, and add it to prove-gates' table if that is how lints are proven here. A site outside the declared files is a scope widening, not a skip.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test__scoped_commit.py: a refused commit whose 2 KB hook output starts with lint-staged's preamble and ends with '✖ prettier --check found issues in lib/store.ts' records a withdrawn row whose details contain lib/store.ts

tasks.title: No gate or config value is rewritten by the write scrub, and every redaction is journaled
tasks.description: PRIORITY (P122-R13). `_manifest_io.scrubbed_plan` runs `_machine_paths.scrubbed_values` over the WHOLE plan on every save (`atomic_write_json`, `save_plan_json`, `save_sharded`, `save_single_file`), so executable and config values are rewritten with everything else: a `meta.buildCommands` entry naming an interpreter under a home directory becomes the outside-repo token and the gate stops running, and with `--project-dir` below the checkout root an in-repo absolute path becomes checkout-relative while gate steps run with cwd=project. Invariant: an executable or config value is never silently rewritten - it is refused at the door that sets it, or exempt from the scrub. Do both: (1) exempt those fields from `scrubbed_plan` by their POSITION in the plan (`meta.buildCommands.*`, `meta.phaseGate`, `meta.fullGate`, each phase's `testGate`, each task's `tests.gate`, and any other field the plan executes - enumerate them from the readers of `_evidence_io.resolved_commands`), as a pointer table beside `scrubbed_plan`, never a key name at any depth (the flaw R11 removed from the ledger); (2) refuse a machine path in those fields at every door that writes them - audit-task's `--gate` on `add`, `scope`, `add-phase` and `retarget`, the panel settings save of `meta.buildCommands` through `_panel_write`, and derive-phase-gate's derived entry - each refusal naming the field and the remedy (a repo-relative or PATH-resolved spelling), with `tools/check-committed-pii.py` left as the backstop for a hand edit. (P122-R14) `scrubbed_values(keep=)` is a name-keyed exemption with no caller outside the mp8 case: replace it with the pointer exemption or delete it with mp8. (P122-R3, P122-R12) A save that redacts prose must say so: only `_panel_write`'s route journals `plan.redact`, while `_proposals._save`, audit-task's own `save_single_file` call, `_evidence_io`'s `save_plan_json` calls, `close-phase._revalidated_write` and migrate-manifest drop the pointers the writer returns. Make the journal row part of the one writer contract (route them through `_panel_write.save_in_layout`, or have every plan writer journal what it redacted) rather than a duty each caller remembers, and add a case over the committed corpus listing the rewrites the scrub makes today, so rewriting historic prose is a decision on record. (prep note) `_invariants.write_baseline` stores each breach's free-text line and its `subject` through the same scrubbing `atomic_write_json`: establish whether a subject or breach line can carry an absolute path, and make the baseline's match key survive the scrub (compare scrubbed keys on both sides, or keep subjects path-free and say so in `found()`), since a subject the scrub rewrote would never match again and re-report a frozen breach as new. Update SECURITY.md's scrub paragraph to the new rule. Faults: P122-R13, P122-R3, P122-R12, P122-R14, prep-invariants-baseline-breach.

tasks.title: Every migrated stub asks selftest_requested(), and the lint sees a local argv name too
tasks.description: P122.8 added `_output.selftest_requested(argv)` and `selftest_argv_violations()`, whose docstring says it cannot see a stub that reads `--selftest` off a local name bound to `sys.argv`. Four stubs do exactly that (`if "--selftest" in argv:` in migrate-manifest's, merge-manifest's, usage/_usage_bench's and render-report's `__main__`). None forwards a command today, but the invariant was every stub. Convert the four to `selftest_requested(...)`, and widen `selftest_argv_violations()` to flag a membership test of `--selftest` against any name bound from `sys.argv` (including a slice) inside a migrated stub, with its prove-gates row (red: plant `argv = sys.argv[1:]` / `"--selftest" in argv` in one stub; allow: the helper call). Faults: P122-R5.

tasks.title: A fix batch lands whole from stdin, rerun re-measures, and fix refusals say the truth
tasks.description: (F606) `drive-phase.add_fix_tasks` calls `audit-task.py add` once per finding and passes the finding's issue and resolution on argv as `--description`; the argv prose check refused a text holding " :400" ("whitespace before a mark that hugs the word in front of it") and the batch stopped with only some findings given a task. Hand the whole batch over in ONE `add --from-file -` call on stdin, where no shell rewrites a value: add `fixes` to `BATCH_TASK_KEYS` so a batch task writes `task.fixes` and each finding's `fixTask` in the same write `--fixes` does today, and the batch lands all or nothing. (F607, the discipline half only - the every-path scope half is P124's b3) a fix task defaults to gate-only, so a finding asking for a new test got gate [lint, typecheck]. Derive a fix task's mode with the rule `--bug` already uses (`_bug_tests_mode`: every named file a test path -> regression with its note, else tdd); gate-only only when the caller passes it. (F608, recurred on P4) `--answer rerun` on a gate-red decision returns None and the next task gate reuses the red verdict ("GATE VERDICT REUSED ... nothing ran here"), so the decision comes back unchanged and the operator ran `run-test-gate.py --no-reuse --record` by hand. A rerun answer measures: mark it in the drive state for that start and pass `--no-reuse` to the next gate run, consuming the mark once. (P122-R15) the `--answer fix` refusal prints "not open: F" for a finding that is open but already names a fix task - say that it already names a fix task and is dispositioned at sign-off; reword the `run_signoff` comment that still says "a finding no fix task names", and drop the guard that restates `accepted-open`/`carried` after `open_findings` (now in `_manifest_phases`) has already excluded them. Name the batch form in verbs-in-full.md and the rerun rule in orchestrator.md. Also F617: a pending triage is satisfied without an answer once every med+ open finding names a pending/in-progress fix task (added by hand with add --fixes); the drive runs them, re-reviews, re-triages; such a finding is offered neither fix nor accept-open. Faults: F606, F607, F608, P122-R15, F617.

(F611) executors twice ended without running the brief's submit block and printed the return object instead. `drive-phase.advance` already turns this into `decide no-executor-return` with answers retry/block, and retry spends an attempt on work that is finished. Add a `resume` answer, recommended and spending no attempt, that prints one instruction: resume the dispatched executor (its id from the dispatch mark) and run its submit block. In the brief, put the submit block first and alone in the closing "Your return" section (`executor_return_lines`), ahead of the return's shape. Keep the decision vocabulary in step with the README's followed table (`_refs.followed_anchor_drift`) and orchestrator.md. tasks.title: A task commit carries exactly its attempt: no older dirt swept in, no new file left out
tasks.description: One invariant: a task's commit holds the change its own attempt made - nothing from before the attempt is swept in, and nothing made during it is left out in silence. (F610) P2.7 was blocked with edits uncommitted in a file P2.8 also declares, and P2.8 started with no warning; on P5 commit-task-work did stage a blocked task's dirty hunks into another task's commit. P122.4's leftover refusal misses it because the edits are covered by the new task's own files. `start` refuses when a declared file of the task being started is dirty and is declared by another not-done task that has spent an attempt (blocked, or in_progress), naming that task and offering unblock-and-finish or a stash named by the task; commit-task-work refuses when a declared file's uncommitted change predates the task's `startedAt` (record at `start` a snapshot of the declared files' blob ids and compare against it; a file mtime is only a fallback, with that basis stated), and where it can, stages only hunks that differ from the start snapshot. (F612 part a, the commit-time check - not guard reading) P4.3's executor `cp`-ed an image outside its declared files; commit-task-work staged declared files only, so the commit references an image it does not contain. `_uncommitted_leftovers` blames only paths the task's files cover: at commit-task-work and at `done --commit` also list untracked or changed paths that appeared since the attempt began and that no in_progress task covers, and refuse naming them, offering `/audit:task scope` widening or removing the file. (P122-R10) `_porcelain_paths` reads `git status --porcelain` without -z, so a path with a space or a non-ASCII byte is quoted and never matches a declared entry: use -z and split on NUL, a rename carrying two names. Update execute-task.md, verbs-in-full.md and the README's /audit:task start/done text. Faults: F610, F612, P122-R10.

tasks.title: A shell-created file outside every running task's scope is refused at the edit tools' tier
tasks.description: (F612 part b - guard command reading) guard-bash-writes' Bash branch filters new dirty paths through `_config.source_exts`, so a `cp` of a .webp outside every in_progress task's scope drew nothing, and even a source file draws only a non-blocking notice whatever tier the plan gate is in; the executor said "plan gate did not refuse". Match the Write/Edit tier: while the gate is in its deny tier (a phase in_progress), a new non-exempt file a shell command created outside every in_progress task's scope is reported whatever its extension, with a blocking PostToolUse decision naming the path and the remedy (remove it, or widen scope with `/audit:task scope`), and recorded in the session state so attempt-bound-commit's check reads the same fact; the warn and observe tiers keep today's notice. Where the command's destination is readable before the diff (cp/mv/install/tee/redirect targets, through the shared `_config` readers), attribute the file to that command; an unreadable command stays attributed by the git-status diff as today. Red-first both directions: `cp a.webp public/x.webp` outside scope in the deny tier -> blocking decision; the same path inside scope, an exempt path, a read-only command and another session's file -> nothing new. Run `tools/bench-hooks.py --gate` after. Faults: F612. GUARD COMMAND-READING CODE: written by the orchestrator with the user's permission (auto mode off when possible); if the API refuses, record it verbatim and hand the remainder to the human.

tasks.title: Every evidence and journal ts ordering goes through one moment reader, held by a lint
tasks.description: (F530) readers order or compare evidence/journal `ts` as TEXT outside `_evidence_io.oldest_first/newest_row/stamp_moment`, all confirmed on main: `_gate_derive` (newest failed row per phase, `>=` on text), `_doctor_trail` (full-scope candidates sorted on `str(ts)`), `_evidence_view` (`sorted(... str(ts) ...)`), `_doctor_completions` (`min(str(ts))` watermark), `_journal_io` (read order, merge interleave, `max` on text at two sites); `_evidence_io._epoch` is a further moment parser (Z form only), and `_classified` SKIPS a windowless other row (`if o_start is None: continue`), so `contested_by`/`shared_the_machine` answer as if that run never happened; `run-test-gate` spells 'did this run pass' inline (`res["status"] == "passed"` on its --json paths) instead of `_evidence_io.row_is_red`. tasks.title: A --record run that stored nothing exits non-zero; a reused verdict repeats its banners
tasks.description: (F532) `run-test-gate --record` wraps `_ev.record(...)` in `except Exception`, prints 'evidence: NOT recorded - ...', then prints GATE GREEN and exits by `res['status']` alone (both the task/phase path and `_record_full_run`), so a pre-push/CI step reading the exit code passes with no evidence. Exit codes are outside COMPATIBILITY's promise but each change is recorded there: give an unrecorded --record run a non-zero exit (a distinct code, named in --help and the docs' exit tables), unchanged without --record. (F565) a verdict reused at an unchanged tree prints 'GATE GREEN: verdict reused from run X; no check ran here.' and none of the banners the measured run printed (NO OVERLAP WITH THIS WORK, TREE CHANGED OUTSIDE THIS WORK, ...), so drive-phase never asks `decide gate-coverage` about it. Store the banner set on the evidence row when the run is measured (`_evidence_io.row_for` allow-list) and have the reuse path print the banners of the run it reuses. (P122-R4) `run-test-gate._declared_by` was switched to `_task_outputs.covers()` and no case exercises it: reverting it to exact match leaves the suite green. Add a case with a `:12-20` line-range entry and a directory entry through `classify_mutations`. Regression: a --record run whose ledger file holds a non-UTF-8 byte exits non-zero; the same run without --record exits 0; a reused NO OVERLAP run prints NO OVERLAP again. Faults: F532, F565, P122-R4.

tasks.title: Red-first helper reads replacements right, derives --introduces, and marks its own block
tasks.description: (F535) `stamp-verification._replaces` reads Assign/AugAssign/AnnAssign targets and setattr only: a `for New.<case> in [...]` or `with ... as New.<case>` target also replaces the case and HEAD's red is still credited through it, while a bare `New.<case>: int` (AnnAssign with no value, binds nothing) is refused. Read For/AsyncFor and With/AsyncWith targets as replacements; count an AnnAssign only with a value; PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE tells an author to wrap with the decorator form. (F573) executors rarely pass `--introduces`, so a test red on a missing symbol grades could-not-prove; have `drive-phase.py submit` derive the introduced symbols from the task's diff (new top-level def/class/assignment names in the declared source files) and pass them to the red helper, with the executor brief naming the flag only as an override. (F576) `_filed_returns.helper_red_first` recognises the helper's block by its wording, so a hand-typed block in those words is filed as computed; `drive-phase.py submit` marks the block it fills (a `source` field or the helper output's digest) and the filing verb trusts the mark, not the words. Regression: T3/T4 (for/with targets) refused; bare annotation proves; a missing-symbol red with no flag grades proved when the diff introduces the symbol; a hand-typed block in the helper's words is not treated as the helper's. Also F613 (testbed P3.1/P5.2/P6.1, and this repo P124.1): a JS missing-module failure (Vite "Failed to resolve import", jest "Cannot find module", node ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND) whose path resolves to a declared file is a missing-symbol red - one per-runner table of missing-module spellings, not a second Python-only list. Also the house runner shape seen on this repo in P124.1/P124.2: a suite whose body aborts on the missing symbol (an AttributeError or TypeError from the task's new name, printing SELFTEST FAILED: N-1/N) is graded "no test was collected or none reached an assertion"; an abort naming the task's introduced symbol, or a declared file, is a missing-symbol red. And: --introduces refuses a hyphenated entry-point name (integrate-task), so a new CLI script cannot name its own symbol; a new file the task declares (untracked at HEAD) is itself the introduced thing. Faults: F535, F573, F576, F613.

tasks.description: With docs/audit/evidence excluded (e.g. via .git/info/exclude), a landing from the branch's own checkout merges and then exits 1 because `commit_landing`/`_commit_stamp` refuses an ignored record path ('the stamp is NOT committed'); the irreversible step has already happened. tasks.title: validate-manifest rejects every plan the published schema rejects, and never raises
tasks.description: (F548 class) `validate-manifest.py` never applies the JSON Schema: `_manifest_crossrefs` types bug values only (`SCHEMA_READ`, `schema_check`), so any verb can write a schema-invalid plan and only CI's ajv step sees it. Add a stdlib validator for the keyword subset `audit-plan.schema.json` uses (new module `manifest/_json_schema.py` with the five things CLAUDE.md lists: a `--selftest` contract whose cases live in tests/, `safe_stdio()` first in `__main__`, a `_deps.LAYERS` placement, a PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE tree line and section, the `_output.PATH_PREAMBLE`; and the migrated-file lists test__output's sc11/sc13 pin), apply it to the whole plan in validate-manifest, and fold the bug-only reader into it; measure the per-verb cost first. (F551) `_manifest_crossrefs._index_bugs` (`bug_by_id`) and `_check_bugs` (`bug['taskId'] not in task_ids`) hash the value, so a list/object id or taskId raises TypeError -> 'internal validator error' naming no field; guard with isinstance so the schema finding names the field. `_manifest_vocab._check_ado` refuses `ado.id: 7.0`, which draft 2020-12 admits: decide (admit an integral float, or keep and say so in the finding). (F552) fallback consumers (`set-priority.py`, `derive-phase-gate.py`, `_panel_write`'s validate before `save_in_layout`, `_proposals._revalidate`) call `validate()` with schema=None and write anyway - bind the loaded schema beside `load_validation_schema` in `_manifest_rules` and use it there (or state the split in COMPATIBILITY's broken-install clause); `ecma_pattern` compiles with re.ASCII (narrows \s) and lets `re.error` escape validate() - catch it as schema-unchecked; a non-object schema or an unresolvable bug item loads as success - treat as unreadable; `_panel_state._cores` docstring says audit-task reads it '(twice)' - delete the count. Regression: parity case running validate-manifest against the starter, the dogfood plan, the examples and planted schema violations (null where a string is required, wrong enum, extra key where additionalProperties is false) - each rejected exactly where ajv rejects; list id / object taskId produce a named finding, never a raise. The finding `$def` gains its keys in findings-record first, so whole-plan validation does not reject the findings `done`/`signoff` write. Faults: F548, F551, F552.

(F316) ratio claims the lint deliberately cannot read: `_deps.py` ('Fourteen of the fifteen sites are converted'), `tests/_harness.py` header ('17 of the 18 detail-carrying files'), `test_remind_tdd.py` docstring ('Twelve of the 48 suites'), `test__panel_page.py` ('# 8 of 40 can be coloured.', 'fails at 17 of 353 with this feature switched off', and the label 'a fixed 3 left 10 of the 72, 6 left 5, 8 left 2, 16 left none'), plus the twin comment in `ui/panel/usage-model.js` ('when only 8 of 40 can be coloured'). Repair is the rule's own: delete the number and keep the pointer; the `test__panel_page.py` measurement table is made a value the case computes and prints in its detail rather than reworded. The lint fixtures in test__output.py/test__deps.py that quote these phrases are inputs and stay, and so does the quotation in `_output.py`'s own WHAT IT CANNOT SEE comment, which documents the shape. (F544a) the `_worktrees` LAYERS comment in `_deps.py` says 'FOUR surfaces need the SAME answer' and names four importers while more import it - delete the count, keep the reason (more than one layer needs the same answer). (F562) CLAUDE.md says `_numeral_span()` 'reads both spellings, for every shape it knows' while its docstring says bare number words under ten are off by default - state the exception and point at the docstring's reason. Regression: the prose lints stay green and `grep -nE "Fourteen of the fifteen|17 of the 18|Twelve of the 48|8 of 40|17 of 353|10 of the 72"` over non-fixture files is empty. Faults: F316, F544, F562.

tasks.title: Every layer number written in prose is checked against _deps.LAYERS or not written
tasks.description: P122.9 gave `_machine_paths` a layer of its own, so every running-prose mention of another module's layer above it - "`name` (layer N)", "`name` (LN)" - is now one too low (some were already off by two). Measured on main at 9b9b9dd1 by matching those two shapes against `_deps.LAYERS`: 116 stale mentions in 25 files, most of them in `_deps.py`'s own LAYERS comments; the prep note's 'seven doctor/gate docstrings' was the visible tip. `layer_doc_drift` (lyd1) grades only a module's OPENING 'Layer N' claim about itself and leaves running prose alone on purpose, which is exactly where the rot sits - the F-prose class of a number a table already holds. Invariant: a layer number in prose is checked or not written. Add the check for every mention shape it can read reliably ("`name` (layer N)", "`name` (LN)", "this file (LN)") in docstrings and comments under scripts/ and hooks/, beside `layer_doc_drift` in `_deps.py`, with a prove-gates row (red: plant a wrong number; allow: a correct one). Repair by deleting the number wherever the layer is not the argument (keep the pointer to the module), and correcting it where the sentence's argument is the layer. Re-derive the count with the new check, never from this description. Faults: prep-layer-prose.

tasks.title: The history guard reads git only in command position and quoted << as data
tasks.description: Probed on main (`git_invocations`): `echo attempt used git stash` -> [('stash', [])] and `cat <<'EOF' | python3 x.py --technical -` with stash words in the body -> stash push (false denies, F505); `sh -c 'echo "a<<b"; git stash drop'` and `sh -c 'echo a<<b; git stash drop'` -> [] (F536: `_config.split_heredocs` treats `<<` inside a single-quoted -c argument as a heredoc and drops the rest - a missed git call). Fix: a git invocation counts only in command position (start, ;, &&, ||, |, newline, or after a command-running prefix found by `_config.program_candidates`); a piped heredoc body is classified by the far side of the pipe (a script reading `-` = data, a shell = commands, unknown = conservative); `split_heredocs` ignores `<<` inside quotes as the shell does. Red-first both directions: `true && git stash push`, `sudo git stash drop`, `xargs git stash drop` stay deny; the two F505 shapes allow; the quoted-<< git call is read. Check `tools/bench-hooks.py --gate` after. Faults: F505, F536. GUARD COMMAND-READING CODE: written by the orchestrator with the user's permission (auto mode off when possible); if the API refuses, record it verbatim and hand the remainder to the human.

Also take any product fail-open the spaced-paths triage hands over (a guard reading a quoted spaced path wrongly). Red-first each. Also F614: a shell-write refusal names the rule that refused it (the plan gate), not the hook that hosts the check. Faults: F542, F547, F614. tasks.title: The release guard finds git and gh past assignments, wrappers, global options and sh -c
tasks.description: Probed on main (`_publishers`): `GH_REPO=x gh release create v1`, `env GH_REPO=x gh release create v1`, `git --git-dir=.git tag v1`, `git -c user.name=x tag v1`, `sudo git tag v1` and `bash -c 'git tag v3'` all return [] - missed denies; `-C`, subshells, heredoc data, quoted text and the listing forms are already handled (the heredoc/listing/unrelated-repo halves of F524 are closed on main). Find the program past leading assignments and wrappers with `_config.program_candidates`, accept git's global options (`-C`, `-c`, `--git-dir=`, `--work-tree=`, ...) before the verb, and read `sh -c`/`bash -c`/eval arguments with `_config.handed_commands`. Deny half first, every spelling above pinned red-first; then confirm the allow cases (`grep 'git tag' f`, heredoc text, `git tag --sort=-creatordate`) stay allowed. `tools/bench-hooks.py --gate` after. Faults: F524. GUARD COMMAND-READING CODE: written by the orchestrator with the user's permission (auto mode off when possible); if the API refuses, record it verbatim and hand the remainder to the human.

tasks.title: the plan gate's free-file budget is per task attempt for subagents, and a refusal names who spent it
tasks.description: F616: require-plan's one-free-file-per-session budget is shared by every subagent an orchestrator session dispatches, so an early executor spends it for every later one, and the refusal names a file the current executor never edited. Key the budget per task attempt for an edit made under a dispatched task (session id plus the in_progress task the edit is covered toward or the driver state names), keep the per-session budget for the main loop, and have the refusal name the task or agent that spent it and when. The directory-entry half of the report is already fixed by P122's covers() (step 3 runs before the done-owner check). Plan-gate hook code, not shell-command parsing. Faults: F616.

tasks.title: a wave executor's submit files against the phase tree's plan from wherever it is run
tasks.description: F619, found live in P123's first wave: the brief's submit block names docs/audit/audit-plan.json relatively and the brief's rule makes every command start with cd <task tree>, so the manifest resolves to the task tree's committed shard where the task is still pending, and audit-task refuses the filing as "records no start".
